subject.title: Add confirmation step to /new and /reset to prevent accidental session wipes

question: Should typed `/new` and hard `/reset` require confirmation by default, and should that policy be configurable?
rationale: Current behavior intentionally treats typed commands as deliberate, while this request changes cross-surface UX and may add public config, so automation should not choose the product policy alone.

options.title: Confirm hard typed resets by default
options.body: Add a single safe confirmation for typed `/new` and hard `/reset` across Control UI and TUI while keeping `/reset soft` unblocked and deferring config until user demand proves it is needed.

options.title: Add configurable confirmation policy
options.body: Implement confirmation plus a documented config option with schema, defaults, and doctor/docs follow-through for existing users.

options.title: Keep typed commands unconfirmed
options.body: Close or narrow this request to already-solved button affordances and keep typed slash commands as explicit power-user actions.

recommendation.title: Confirm hard typed resets by default
recommendation.body: Add a single safe confirmation for typed `/new` and hard `/reset` across Control UI and TUI while keeping `/reset soft` unblocked and deferring config until user demand proves it is needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The current confirmation behavior and explicit typed-command scope came through PR 73361, making this the closest history-backed owner for the UX decision.
